spider_synthesis.finding_1: PROTEST alone is not predictive of internet shutdown. Georgia and Serbia experienced very large/repeated protests without an established systematic shutdown pattern.
spider_synthesis.finding_2: Network architecture matters. Belarus combines strong state gateway centralization with repeated cross-provider protest/election restrictions; this is the cleanest positive control in the set.
spider_synthesis.finding_3: Technology lineage is not mechanism identity. Belarus combines Russian SORM architecture with Sandvine DPI; Kazakhstan combines Russian SORM lineage with reported Allot DPI; therefore Russian surveillance lineage cannot be used as a shortcut to attribute active filtering technology.
spider_synthesis.finding_4: Repressive states can choose different technical layers. Belarus/Kazakhstan show path-level connectivity controls; Serbia shows targeted device surveillance and a separate RF/GNSS interference candidate; Georgia shows legal/physical pressure with no systematic shutdown baseline.
spider_synthesis.finding_5: The strongest causal signature is EVENT -> NETWORK POLICY CHANGE -> EVENT END/PHASE CHANGE -> RECOVERY, replicated across independent telemetry and localized to operator/path. Political coincidence without network localization is insufficient.
spider_synthesis.finding_6: A Russian remote-control hypothesis remains unproven across all four countries. The current graph supports capability diffusion/supply-chain/architectural analogies, not a common Moscow-operated control plane.

cisa_gate.reason: Historical domestic repression and technology lineage are not enough. No current incident yet satisfies the full foreign-vantage U.S.-service/path-specific/control-plane bridge contract.
minimum_unlock_bundle: Current foreign-vantage failure affecting a stable basket of U.S./open services while provider-side health remains normal.
ASN/operator/path localization with matched alternate-path control.
Independent replication from at least two measurement families, e.g. OONI plus IODA/RIPE/Cloudflare/provider telemetry.
Policy-like selectivity such as deny/allowlist, protocol-specific blocking, or stable middlebox fingerprint rather than generic congestion/outage.
A real cross-border or control-plane bridge. Vendor lineage alone is insufficient; remote management, common configuration, synchronized multi-country behavior, or equivalent evidence is required.
Explicit falsifiers: ordinary provider outage, power failure, crowd-cell congestion, local legal blocking, and destination-service incident must be tested first.

Kazakhstan has a repeated historical protest/network-control correlation.
Georgia and Serbia are useful negative controls for the proposition that protests automatically cause shutdowns.
